plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Increase QQQI to 25% to favor income and broad index exposure.
Increase QQQ to 20% to further favor broad index exposure.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a target of ~1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest returns.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 1% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Buy CCJ at 4% to add a strong risk/reward long setup.
Buy ORCL at 3% to add another strong risk/reward long setup.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a small leveraged ETF presence.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding high-quality scanner setups. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a blend of broad market and quality tech exposure.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the concentration mandate.
Add SOXL to 6% and SPAL to 6% to increase leveraged ETF exposure.
Buy CCJ at 6% to lean into a high-scoring scanner setup.
Buy RGTI at 5% to further concentrate in high-scoring setups.
This plan aggressively seeks growth by using leverage and concentrating in strong setups.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware this approach carries substantially higher risk, including larger potential drawdowns and the impact of daily leverage decay/rebalancing.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Add QQQI to 30% to prioritize income and covered-call ETFs.
Increase QQQ to 20% to maintain some broad index exposure.
This plan focuses on generating steady monthly distributions with lower growth.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month, aiming to park cash for yield. It prioritizes income-generating ETFs and broad index exposure, cutting high-beta single names and leverage. While aiming for steady distributions, remember these are variable, and NAV can still decline in market selloffs.
